sub_theme: Compass Directions and Our School Grounds

lessons.title: Non-Fiction: How Compasses Work
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about compasses from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about compasses.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real or picture compass.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about how compasses work.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a compass (real or on a phone app) at home.

lessons.title: Quarter Turns and Compass Directions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to link quarter turns to compass direction changes.
success_criteria: I can make a quarter turn.
I can say which compass direction I'm now facing.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model making quarter turns and relating them to compass direction changes (e.g. facing north, quarter turn clockwise faces east).
lessons.independent_task: Children practise making turns and identifying the resulting compass direction.
resources_needed: Floor compass or compass direction cards
key_questions: If you face north and turn a quarter clockwise, which way do you face?

differentiation.support: Practise with physical turns and adult support
differentiation.greater_depth: Combine multiple turns and predict the final direction

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of turns to compass directions, linking Year 1 and Year 2 geometry — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Practise quarter turns and compass directions at home.

lessons.title: The Four Compass Points Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use the four compass points confidently.
success_criteria: I can name the four compass points.
I can point in each direction.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate the four compass points using a floor compass activity.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise using compass directions to describe positions around the classroom/school.
resources_needed: Floor compass or compass rose diagram

differentiation.greater_depth: Use all four directions confidently and combine with distance

lessons.assessment_notes: Consolidation check on compass direction use before applying to the school grounds — evidence for GEOG.2.

lessons.title: Writing Directions Around the School
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write clear directions using compass points.
success_criteria: I can write a direction using a compass point.
I can use sequencing words.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing directions around the school using compass points and sequencing words.
lessons.independent_task: Children write directions from one place to another around the school using compass points.
key_questions: Which direction do you go first?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing combined with compass vocabulary — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share directions with a partner and follow them.
lessons.home_link: Give directions using compass points at home.

lessons.title: Compass Direction Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve problems involving compass directions and turns.
success_criteria: I can work out a final direction after turns.
I can explain my reasoning.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap turns and compass directions from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving problems involving a sequence of turns from a starting direction.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve compass/turn problems, explaining their reasoning.
key_questions: If you start facing east and turn twice, which way do you face?
How did you work it out?

differentiation.support: Use a physical compass/turns to work out answers

lessons.assessment_notes: Record application of turns and directions to problem-solving — evidence for MATHS.GEO.

lessons.title: Surveying Our School Grounds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to survey and record features of the school grounds using compass directions.
success_criteria: I can identify a feature's compass direction.
I can record it accurately.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the school grounds features from Week 2.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model surveying the school grounds, recording features and their compass direction from a fixed point.
lessons.independent_task: Children survey the school grounds (or use provided data/photos), recording features and directions.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note fieldwork skill combining compass directions with observation — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Identify the compass direction of something from your home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Compass Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read compass-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read compass words.
I can read a sentence about direction.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to compass-themed words (e.g. 'north', 'south', 'turn').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading compass words over the week.

lessons.title: School Grounds Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a school grounds context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a school grounds survey context (e.g. trees counted in different areas).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve school-grounds-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a school grounds word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Creating a Compass Map of the School
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a map of the school grounds showing compass directions.
success_criteria: I can draw the school grounds.
I can add a compass rose showing directions.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the school grounds survey from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a map of the school grounds including a compass rose.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own map of the school grounds, adding a compass rose and key features.
key_questions: Where does north go on your map?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of map-making and compass direction skills — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Share compass maps of the school.
lessons.home_link: Show your compass map to your family and explain the directions.

lessons.title: Giving Compass Direction Instructions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to give and follow instructions using compass directions.
success_criteria: I can give an instruction using a compass direction.
I can follow an instruction accurately.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap compass directions used this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model giving instructions using compass directions (e.g. 'walk two steps north').
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns giving and following compass direction instructions in the school grounds or classroom.
key_questions: Did you follow the instruction correctly?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and practical application of compass directions — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Play a compass direction instruction game at home.

lessons.title: Compass Direction Survey Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record and interpret data about compass direction preferences.
success_criteria: I can record a tally.
I can interpret the results.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a simple survey (e.g. which direction is your favourite classroom display facing), recording data.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct and interpret a simple compass-related survey.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation applied to a geography context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple survey with your family.

lessons.title: Compass Directions Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about compass directions and the school grounds.
success_criteria: I can name the four compass points.
I can use them to describe a location.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about compass directions.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Compass Directions' display combining maps, surveys, and instructions from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about compass directions?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, completing the geography skills unit — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about compass directions with your family.

lessons.title: Compass Directions Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about compass directions.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about compasses and directions, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: How does a compass help travellers?
Why might sailors have used compasses long ago?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on compass facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Turns, Directions, Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply turns, compass direction and data skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can work out a direction after a turn.
I can read survey data.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's turns, directions, and data learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: turns/directions, data handling.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 32 maths observations for each child, completing the geometry/geography crossover unit — evidence for MATHS.GEO/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising compass directions over the weekend.
